q: If a human cell is deprived of oxygen, which stages of respiration stop?
options: Only oxidative phosphorylation; the Krebs cycle carries on making ATP and reduced NAD
Oxidative phosphorylation, the Krebs cycle and the link reaction; only glycolysis continues
Glycolysis stops first, because it needs O2 to act as the final hydrogen acceptor for its NAD
No stage stops completely; all four stages simply continue more slowly than before
explanation: O2 is used directly only at complex IV, but all mitochondrial stages depend on it indirectly: without O2 the ETC stops, NADH and FADH2 can't be reoxidised, and the link reaction and Krebs cycle – which need NAD+ and FAD – stop as well. Glycolysis continues only because converting pyruvate to lactate regenerates NAD+.
